correctness.rationale: The dihedral multiplication law yields the graph decompositions exactly. A two-dimensional symmetric bilinear representation gives a rank-two graph-pattern matrix in both parity cases. Every possible pair of omitted vertices is analyzed: mixed pairs always force; two rotations never force; two reflections force exactly when they do not commute. Thus the \(N-2\) forcing sets and their counts are complete. The inequality \(M(G)\le Z(G)\) closes \(\operatorname{mr}(G)=2\) and \(M(G)=Z(G)=N-2\), and the \(N-1\) and \(N\) coefficients are immediate.

value.rationale: The finding gives a complete minimum-zero-forcing-set classification and the entire zero forcing polynomial of a canonical finite-group graph. The leading coefficient changes with the parity-sensitive commuting relation among reflections, so the enumeration retains group structure rather than being a bare graph-order count. The explicit rank-two witnesses tie this classification to maximum nullity and inverse-eigenvalue theory.
